result:
Round 222 passes. A's fix works in a real browser: on the purchased-Studio page, the Export dialog now opens with all 10 stems ticked and "Export Audio" enabled, at both 1440×900 and 1280×720. Before the fix it was 0 of 10. I recorded `browserVerified` and `realVerified` as true.

One criterion was not met as written, and B needs to rule on it. The task wanted the default-selection WAV and the "Select All" WAV to be byte-identical or have identical audio data. They are not identical: 284 of about 384,000 samples differ by the smallest possible step (1 LSB). A control run shows this is not caused by the fix. Two exports with the same untouched selection also differ, in 318 samples. Every stem measures the same level in both files, so the default really does equal "Select All". I suggest B change the criterion to "within 1 LSB plus matching per-stem levels". This is logged as C-R222-01.

**What was checked**
- **Scope:** HEAD is `6dd45a1`. Only the granted dialog file and the 2 new files changed; all checksums match at start and end. I tested the code changes on a scratch copy outside the repo, and the repo file is unchanged from A's handover.
- **Unit tests:** 7 of 7 pass and the type check is clean.
- **Red-proof:** I made my own broken versions of the dialog code. Restoring the old start-up code fails ES1, ES5, ES6 and ES7. Resetting the selection on every stem update fails ES3 and ES4.
- **Code:** only the selection logic changed. No layout, wording or handler changes, no `any`, no type assertions.
- **Exports (1440):**
  - The MP3 High file is 168 frames at 320 kbps, intact to the end, and decodes to stereo at 4.032 s, the same as round 221.
  - With one stem (Duduk) unticked, that stem is 80.5 dB quieter than the others in the WAV (30 dB required). Each test stem plays its own tone, matched to the stem by file name, not by download order.
- **Persistence (1280):** I unticked Didgeridoo, then closed and reopened the dialog: still 9 of 10. I then muted a different stem (Duduk) in the mixer and reopened: still 9 of 10 with the same stem unticked, and the button reads "Select All".
- **Select / Deselect All:** works at both sizes (0 of 10 disables Export, 10 of 10 enables it).
- **Ableton tab:** "Download .als" is enabled with 10 of 10 ticked.
- **Studio Lab export:** 24-bit, 48 kHz stereo WAV whose length matches the shown time exactly. Its loudness is −15.29 dBFS, the same as round 221.
- **No sign-in:** in a fresh browser with no credentials, the demo page opens. The purchased page shows "Sign in required" and loads no audio, and the token API returns 401.
- **Implementation doc 174:** headings in order, line 4 exactly as required, and it only cites tests that exist.
- **Not run:** checking real ownership through the backend is blocked, because the backend isn't available in the cloud. The full test suite, build and verify belong to the root gate.

**Ableton comparison:** ticking every stem as the full mix and choosing stems inside the dialog are both deliberate differences from Live. Whether Live has a default here is unconfirmed: I re-checked the manual and it names no default for the Rendered Track option.

**Low findings for B (none caused by A)**
- **C-R222-01:** the old WAV export gives slightly different output each time, even with Normalize off and with no dither or randomness in the code. The cause is not confirmed; my guess is the order floating-point values are added in during rendering.
- **C-R222-02:** doc 174 and B's task both quote the Ableton manual as saying "most users will choose". The manual actually says "This is likely the option you will use for most scenarios". The meaning is close, but it isn't a real quote.
- **C-R222-03:** at 1280×720 the Export dialog's Cancel / Export Audio buttons are cut off and only reachable by scrolling inside it. This was already the case in round 221.

Files are in /home/runner/czaba-project/tmp/studio-real-loop:
- c-round-222.md
- c-round-222.json
- c-round-222/ (scripts, logs, screenshots, exported files)
